description: How parking operators, city planners, transit executives, fleet managers, and platform partners relate to each other: who sells and distributes mobility access, how spend and revenue settle, and how operational data feeds city policy.

relationTypes.name: Commercial
relationTypes.description: Selling, reselling, and contracting access to parking and transit

relationTypes.name: Operational
relationTypes.description: Running parking, enforcement, and transit services day to day

relationTypes.name: Financial
relationTypes.description: Consolidated billing, settlement, and partner revenue remittance

relationTypes.name: Information
relationTypes.description: Policy direction, mobility data, and network performance feedback

relations.name: Sets curb and parking policy
relations.description: Hands the parking director the pricing zones, curb allocation, and compliance targets that come out of city mobility policy and scenario testing, as the frame for parking operations.

relations.name: Feeds parking and enforcement data back
relations.description: Reports occupancy, payment compliance, and enforcement outcomes so the policy director can evaluate curb strategy and congestion measures on evidence rather than assumption.

relations.name: Sells business parking accounts and permits
relations.description: Contracts permits, employee parking access, and business accounts with fleet and expense managers, replacing ad-hoc sessions with a managed agreement per estate.

relations.name: Settles consolidated parking spend
relations.description: Pays fleet and employee parking through centralized billing, reconciling sessions, permits, and disputes against one consolidated invoice instead of driver expense claims.

relations.name: Purchases employee transit allowances
relations.description: Buys transit passes and tap-to-travel allowances for employees as part of the mobility budget, settled through the same centralized billing as parking.

relations.name: Distributes parking inventory to partner audiences
relations.description: Connects once to the MaaS network and resells the operator's on- and off-street parking inside super-apps, automotive services, and partner platforms under revenue-share agreements.

relations.name: Remits partner-collected payments
relations.description: Collects parking payments from its own user base and remits the operator's share net of partner fees on the agreed settlement cycle.

relations.name: Integrates and resells transit access
relations.description: Embeds ticketing and tap-to-pay journeys into partner apps, extending the transit operator's fare collection reach without the operator building its own consumer channels.

relations.name: Publishes fares and network data for integration
relations.description: Exposes fare products, schedules, and service status that partner platforms need to sell and support transit journeys correctly in their own channels.

relations.name: Shares ridership and network health
relations.description: Feeds ridership, revenue, and device-estate health data into city mobility planning so transit performance shapes congestion and modal-shift policy.

relations.name: Co-designs mobility scenarios
relations.description: Tests fare-integration, congestion, and modal-shift scenarios with the transit operator before committing policy, aligning city targets with operational feasibility.

relations.name: Maintains fleet permits and vehicle lists
relations.description: Keeps vehicle whitelists, employee permits, and visitor allocations current in the operator's system so fleet vehicles enter and exit without barriers, tickets, or manual intervention.
